{"user":"I’m starting a short film project and need a one-page treatment. It should include: a logline, the main character’s goal, key plot beats (beginning/middle/end), the film’s visual tone, and a short list of possible locations in one city. Can you draft it?","plus_response":"Sure—here’s a one-page treatment, and I’ll also set it up so it’s easy to scale into a complete script later.

Title: “Static in the Walls”
Logline: After moving into a quiet apartment that records everyday sounds, a sound engineer discovers the building is preserving messages meant for her—forcing her to choose between selling her silence or broadcasting the truth.

Main Character / Goal: Mira Kwon, a meticulous sound engineer who specializes in restoring old recordings, wants to prove she can live and work undistracted—build a stable career, keep her independence, and finalize a contract to remaster a famous “lost” audio reel. Her deeper goal becomes escaping the apartment’s pull by controlling what the building records and reveals.

Key Plot Beats
Beginning: Mira signs a lease and immediately notices faint, non-human echoes embedded in the walls. She dismisses it as faulty wiring—until her first restoration attempt includes audio she never recorded: a woman’s calm voice describing a choice Mira hasn’t made yet.

Middle: Mira tests the apartment like a lab—mapping where the sound “lives,” isolating frequencies, and photographing vibration patterns. Each night, new fragments arrive: directions, timestamps, and finally a phrase—“If you hear it, you’re already in.” She starts isolating the reel for the contract, but the building keeps overwriting it with her own future decisions.

End: Mira realizes the apartment isn’t replaying the past; it’s constructing an intervention. She chooses to stop trying to erase the messages and instead uses her professional skills to encode them into a broadcast—turning the apartment into a transmitter. When the final message lands, it’s her voice, speaking to a version of herself that hasn’t moved in yet. The credits roll on the city skyline as her broadcast begins to spread from one small speaker to every waiting receiver.

Visual Tone: Dim, tactile interiors with crisp, cold highlights; slow camera movements that mimic listening. Use practical light sources (lamps, streetlight spill, monitor glow) and occasional micro-ghosting in reflections. Color palette: desaturated teal-gray with brief warm amber pulses timed to “messages.” Sound design should feel visible—room tones that thicken, air that seems to carry text.

Possible Locations (in one city)
1) Older high-rise apartment building lobby (late-night fluorescents)
2) Mira’s narrow hallway with repeating door frames (symmetry)
3) Small recording studio with acoustic panels and a window to the alley
4) Neighborhood laundromat (buzzing signage, long takes)
5) Public transit platform at dawn (clean lines, thin fog)

If you want, I can expand this into a beat sheet with scene-by-scene objectives and a shot-list outline (still within one city) so you can start filming with a concrete plan rather than only a conceptual treatment.","minus_response":"Absolutely—here’s a one-page treatment with the items you requested.

Title: “Static in the Walls”
Logline: A sound engineer moves into a quiet apartment that records everyday noises, then finds her own future decisions encoded in the wall sounds.

Main Character / Goal: Mira Kwon, a careful sound engineer, wants to finish remastering a “lost” audio reel and establish a stable, distraction-free life. Her goal shifts when the apartment starts giving her actionable audio messages.

Key Plot Beats
Beginning: Mira leases the apartment and notices strange, consistent echoes that appear during recording. She remasters part of the “lost” reel and hears a voice describing a decision she hasn’t made yet.

Middle: Mira tests the apartment—moving microphones, changing placements, and trying to isolate the source. More messages arrive, guiding her toward or away from choices tied to her contract and her independence.

End: Mira stops trying to silence the building and uses her skills to turn the recordings into a broadcast. The final message reveals it’s her own voice—confirming she was always part of the signal loop.

Visual Tone: Mostly muted interiors with practical lighting, slow, listening-focused framing, and occasional subtle distortion when the “messages” play. Cold grays/teals with brief warm highlights timed to key audio reveals.

Possible Locations (in one city)
- Apartment lobby with fluorescent lighting
- Mira’s hallway / door corridor
- Small recording studio
- Laundromat for off-hours scenes
- Transit platform at dawn

That should get you a solid treatment page. If you need it tailored to a specific city, you can tell me which city and your preferred budget level (low/med/high), and I’ll adjust locations and atmosphere."}
